ringtone noun

also ring tone, ring (of a phone)

* our formation

* (our own formation) sonus, sonī m.

noun, second declension

the sound a phone makes when it rings

No reference work has a word for a ringtone. The phone rings with sonāre (see the phone is ringing; Andresian p. 14), so the sound it rings with is its sonus, the plain classical word for a sound; sonus tēlephōnī where it must be said whose.

Other words

  • * (our own formation) tinnītus, tinnītūs m. — a ringing, jingling

    noun, fourth declension · also used · * our formation · Verg. G. 4.64; Ov. Met. 5.204 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica: Verg., Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā post Augustum (Sen., Plin.))

    Classically the ring of bronze and cymbals, so apt for a bell-like tone.

See also the phone is ringing, telephone, notification.

SourcesLewis & Short: sonus · Lewis & Short: tinnitus

Anna Andresian, Vocabula Picta (2014), p. 14: sonō for a ringing phone.
